Reviewed p50/p95 latency, steady-state throughput, and the impact of KV/prefix caching and batching. Decided on next bench runs and agreed to evaluate a short Dedicated pilot if numbers hold.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Arianna Park (Redwood AE), Luis Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (StreamlineAI - Dir MLOps), Tom Reynolds (StreamlineAI - CTO), Jin Soo Park (StreamlineAI - SRE)
Shared artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (drive: /benchmarks/streamline-benchmark-2025-11-08.xlsx), runbook link noted in chat

[00:00] Arianna: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, hope you all had a good week. Quick check-in  agenda is to run through the latest benchmark numbers vs your baseline provider, talk through tuning, and agree next steps. Luis, you want to kick off with the numbers?

[00:18] Luis: Yeah sure. So we re-ran the suite on 11/08 and again yesterday after enabling the kv cache and a small batching window. Quick note  warmup was 2k tokens, steady-state measured over 5 minutes. The baseline provider numbers (your side) were p50 ~ 95ms, p95 ~ 290ms for the 512-token seq workload and throughput around 110 requests per second.

[00:47] Maya: Just to confirm, baseline is what we ran from the vendor last week with their default 16-bit model right?

[00:54] Luis: Right, default FP16. For Redwood in the POC config  quantized 4-bit, kernel optimizations, and KV caching on  we're seeing p50 ~ 68ms, p95 ~ 145ms, and throughput about 185 rps for identical payloads. That's with a 16ms batching window and a conservative concurrency target.

[01:20] Tom: That's a pretty big gap at p95. Is that with real logging/eviction on the cache? I want to make sure it's not an artifact of synthetic warm cache.

[01:30] Luis: Good call. The reported numbers were a mix  we did a cold run and warm-run. Cold p95 does rise closer to 230ms, which is closer to baseline, but steady-state warm cache is where we see the 145ms. We added notes in the sheet marking which runs were warm.

[01:50] Jin: What's the memory footprint on your 4-bit quantized model? We need to validate it fits our node constraints  64GB GPU memory per node.

[01:57] Luis: With 4-bit quant and some kernel remapping we fit comfortably within 48GB in our test config. The KV cache adds ephemeral memory per request but it's within expected margins. We'll send a memory breakdown.

[02:12] Arianna: I'm going to flag here that the kv is sometimes transcribed as K V cache in the logs, so ignore weird capitalization  transcription quirk.

[02:20] Maya: Ok. Two follow-ups: first, can you show the p95 distribution? We care about tail behavior for interactive UI. Second, can you reproduce the baseline's worst-case, like burst traffic?

[02:33] Luis: Yep, we have histogram plots in the sheet. p95 distribution tightens significantly with KV enabled and smaller batching window. For burst tests we did a ramp to 500 rps  Redwood config held at ~420 rps before we saw queuing; baseline throttled earlier and had higher p95 spikes.

[02:55] Tom: Were those runs on the same GPU instance type? We need apples-to-apples comparison.

[03:02] Luis: We matched closest available: both tests used A10-equivalent type for fairness  there is some variation in driver versions, we documented them. Later we can also run on the exact hardware you have on-prem if you want.

[03:16] Maya: That's helpful. On quality, any differences when using quantization? We noticed in prior POC that 4-bit sometimes hurts sampling on longer sequences.

[03:26] Luis: Good point  we ran a quality diff on your prompt set (sample size 200). For majority of prompts there was no perceivable delta. On ~8% of cases 4-bit had minor tokenization glitches which we flagged; those are often fixable by small temperature/prefix adjustments or we can pin to mixed precision for those paths. We'll include the diff file in the sheet.

[03:50] Jin: For the SRE team, can you share the fallback policy you mentioned, if capacity saturates? We want to avoid tail latency shocks in production.

[03:58] Luis: Yes, we demoed auto-fallback in the Console: if Dedicated pool is full we route to hosted variants or to a smaller model variant, with circuit-breaker thresholds. We'll attach the rollout policy doc.

[04:12] Arianna: Also a note on costs  the Dedicated pilot pricing we sent yesterday covers a small reserved pool plus burst capacity. I'll re-share the updated pricing as an action item.

[04:22] Tom: Curious on batching: you said a 16ms window. If we reduce window to 8ms what's the effect?

[04:28] Luis: Reducing to 8ms lowers throughput slightly but benefits latency p50 by ~8-12ms; p95 improves with cache more than with batching changes. It's a tradeoff: tighter windows favor latency, looser windows favor throughput/cost. We'll include a tuning matrix in the runbook.

[04:47] Maya: For the next run I'd like three configs: (A) Redwood current (4-bit + KV + 16ms), (B) Redwood tighter latency (4-bit + KV + 8ms), (C) Redwood mixed precision fallback for flagged prompts. Also recreate baseline under identical load pattern.

[05:05] Luis: Sounds good  we'll queue those. We'll also run a 95th percentile stability test over 30 minutes to show steady-state.

[05:13] Jin: For security/compliance, Tom asked we get SOC2 docs and a network diagram for private connections if we pursue Dedicated  can you send those?

[05:20] Arianna: Yes, will send SOC2 and the high-level network diagram. For Dedicated we provide VPC peering + KMS options  we'll include the options in the follow-up email.

[05:31] Tom: One more thing  regarding your kernel selection and compilation, can you guarantee identical perf across region? We want to avoid region-to-region variance for our users.

[05:39] Luis: We tune kernel selection per hardware. We can't guarantee byte-for-byte identical latency across regions because instance types and drivers differ, but the runtime will pick optimized kernels to minimize variance. For Dedicated we can run a sanity test across target regions and share expected variance range.

[05:58] Maya: Ok let's recap so we have the same action list.

[06:02] Arianna: Recap: Luis will run the 3 config benchmark + 30-min p95 stability and memory breakdown; Arianna will send pricing and SOC2/network docs; Maya will share final prompt set and sample payloads. We'll follow up on 11/19 to review Dedicated pilot numbers. Anything else?

[06:20] Tom: No, that covers it.

[06:23] Jin: Thanks everyone.

[06:25] Arianna: Thanks all  we'll drop the sheet and runbook into the thread and ping when runs complete. Bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker tag mismatch (Speaker 2 -> Luis), some punctuation is off, we referenced the benchmark sheet multiple times.
